plain: To formally charge a public official with serious wrongdoing

more.text: To accuse; to charge with a crime or misdemeanor; but appropriately, to exhibit charges of maladministration against a public officer before a competent tribunal, that is, to send or put on, to load.
To accuse; to censure; to call in question; as, to impeach one's motives or conduct.
To call to account; to charge as answerable.

example.quote: How, in fact, could a majority in the House of Representatives impeach themselves?
